'''Andrew Alexander Ranicki''' (born '''Andrzej Aleksander Ranicki'''; 30 December 1948 – 21 February 2018) was a British [[mathematician]] who worked on [[algebraic topology]].  He was a professor of mathematics at the [[University of Edinburgh]].

==Life==

Ranicki was the only child of the well-known literary critic [[Marcel Reich-Ranicki]]<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/obituaries/marcel-reich-ranicki-widely-admired-literary-critic-8832965.html%3famp |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/archive/20220507/https://www.independent.co.uk/news/obituaries/marcel-reich-ranicki-widely-admired-literary-critic-8832965.html%3famp |archive-date=7 May 2022 |url-access=subscription |url-status=live |title = Marcel Reich-Ranicki: Widely admired literary critic|website=[[Independent.co.uk]] |date = 2013-09-22}}{{cbignore}}</ref> and the artist Teofila Reich-Ranicki; he spoke Polish in his family.  Born in London, he lived in [[Warsaw]], in [[Frankfurt am Main]] and [[Hamburg]], and attended school in England at the [[King's School, Canterbury]] from the age of sixteen.<ref>[[Emilia Smechowski]]: [http://www.taz.de/1/archiv/digitaz/artikel/?ressort=ku&dig=2014%2F09%2F13%2Fa0084&cHash=7b0339a23ac4e979a9f4584bb53ea3ca „Er hatte die Wucht eines Niagara-Falls“], Interview in [[Die Tageszeitung|TAZ]], 13. September 2014, S. 32 f.</ref><ref>[[Volker Hage]], [[Martin Doerry]]: [http://www.spiegel.de/spiegel/print/d-127194996.html Spiegel-Gespräch: „Ich habe nie gefragt“], [[Der Spiegel]], May 26, 2014</ref><ref name="Tripos">'Cambridge Tripos: English; Medical Sciences; Mathematics', ''Times'', 20 June 1969.</ref>

Ranicki studied Mathematics at [[Trinity College, Cambridge]], and graduated with a BA in 1969.<ref name="Tripos"/> At Cambridge, he was a student of topologists [[Andrew Casson]] and [[John Frank Adams]].<ref>{{MathGenealogyProject | 24513 | name = Andrew Ranicki}}</ref> He earned his doctoral degree in 1973 with a thesis on [[algebra]]ic [[L-theory]]. Ranicki received numerous awards and honors for his scientific achievements during his studies. From 1972 to 1977, he was a [[Fellow]] of Trinity College.<ref>[http://www.maths.ed.ac.uk/~aar/surgery/cvaar.pdf Curriculum Vitae, Andrew Ranicki]</ref>

From 1977 to 1982, he was assistant professor at [[Princeton University]]. In 1982, he began at the [[University of Edinburgh]] as a [[lecturer]]; in 1987, he was promoted to [[Reader (academic rank)|reader]]. In 1992, he became a Fellow of the [[Royal Society of Edinburgh]].<ref>[http://www.royalsoced.org.uk/67_Fellows.html Directory of Fellows] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161020175448/https://www.royalsoced.org.uk/67_Fellows.html |date=2016-10-20 }}, page 33.</ref> From 1995, Ranicki was the Chair of [[Surgery theory|Algebraic Surgery]] at the University of Edinburgh.<ref>[http://www.maths.ed.ac.uk/~aar/surgery/personal.pdf Chair of Algebraic Surgery], University of Edinburgh, Communications and Marketing.</ref> Several times, he stayed as a visiting scientist at the [[Max Planck Institute for Mathematics]] in Bonn, most recently in 2011.<ref>Johannes Seiler: [http://www.mpim-bonn.mpg.de/node/3123 "Mathematics is a drug!" A conversation with Andrew Ranicki], [[Bonner General-Anzeiger]] from January 8–9, 2011 on the website of the [[Max Planck Institute for Mathematics| Max Planck Institute for Mathematics Bonn]]</ref>

==Personal life and death==

Ranicki married American paleontologist Ida Thompson in 1979; they had a daughter. Ranicki suffered from [[leukemia]]; he died peacefully in the presence of his wife.<ref name="Anz">[[Thomas Anz]]: [http://literaturkritik.de/zum-tod-von-andrew-ranicki-sohn-von-teofila-und-marcel-reich-ranicki,24261.html Obituary of Andrew Ranicki], [[literaturkritik.de]], February 22, 2018.</ref>

A conference celebrating his legacy was held at the [[International Centre for Mathematical Sciences]] (Edinburgh) in summer 2020.<ref>{{cite web|title=Manifolds and K-theory: the legacy of Andrew Ranicki|url=https://www.icms.org.uk/manifoldsandktheory.php}}</ref>

==Published works==

* ''Exact sequences in the algebraic theory of surgery,'' Princeton University Press, 1981.
* ''Lower K and L Theory'', London Mathematical Society Lecture Notes, Vol. 178, Cambridge University Press. 1992.
* ''Algebraic L-Theory and Topological Manifolds'', Cambridge Tracts in Mathematics Vol. 102, Cambridge University Press, 1992.
* ''Algebraic and Geometric Surgery'', Oxford University Press, 2002.
* ''High dimensional knot theory '', Springer, 1998.
* with Bruce Hughes: '' Ends of Complexes '', Cambridge Tracts in Mathematics Vol. 123, Cambridge University Press, 1996.
* with [[Norman Levitt]] and [[Frank Quinn (mathematician)|Frank Quinn]]: "Algebraic and geometric topology" (Rutgers University conference, New Brunswick, 1983), Springer 1985, Lecture Notes in Mathematics Vol. 1126.
* Editor with [[David W. Lewis (mathematician)|David W. Lewis]] and [[Eva Bayer-Fluckiger]]: "Quadratic forms and their applications" (Conference Dublin 1999), Contemporary Mathematics Vol. 272, American Mathematical Society, 2000.
* Publisher: '' Noncommutative Localization in Algebra and Topology '', London Mathematical Society Vol. 330, Cambridge University Press, 2006.
* Editor with Steven Ferry and [[Jonathan Rosenberg (mathematician)|Jonathan Rosenberg]]: "The Novikov conjectures, index theorems and rigidity" (Oberwolfach, 1993), London Mathematical Society Lecture Notes, Vol. 226, 227, Cambridge University Press, 1995.
* Editor: ''The Hauptvermutung Book'', Kluwer, 1996.
* Editor with [[Sylvain Cappell]] and [[Jonathan Rosenberg (mathematician)|Jonathan Rosenberg]]: '' Surveys on surgery theory. Papers dedicated to C.T. C. Wall.''
